name: caddy-ui-backend
description: Backend for caddy/ui, a web interface for managing Caddy servers, Caddyfiles, routes, certificates, logs, and metrics. Requires the caddy-ui-frontend container and an existing Caddy server. Select the same user-defined Docker bridge network for both UI containers and Caddy. You can use an existing custom bridge network: change Network Type in both templates to that network. If you need a new network, run "docker network create caddy-ui" in the Unraid terminal before installing and select "Custom: caddy-ui". Keep the container names caddy-ui-backend and caddy-ui-frontend. Enable "admin 0.0.0.0:2019" in Caddy's global configuration block; keep the admin API private. Start the backend before the frontend. Set External UI URL to the exact address used in your browser, including scheme and port, such as http://192.168.1.10:9877. Open the frontend to create the administrator, save the recovery key, and discover or add Caddy instances. Restrict access until initial setup is complete. Configuration and credentials persist in /etc/caddy-ui. The Docker socket grants control of Docker containers and is used for discovery and file operations.

paths.name: Application data
paths.description: Persistent administrator credentials, instances, Caddyfile history, and settings.

paths.name: Docker socket
paths.description: Required for Docker discovery and operations inside Caddy containers. Grants control of the Docker host.

variables.name: External UI URL
variables.description: Required browser-facing frontend URL, including scheme and port, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:9877. Use the external HTTPS URL when behind a reverse proxy. Update this if the frontend address changes.

variables.name: Log level
variables.description: Log verbosity: debug, info, warn, or error.

variables.name: Uptime history retention (days)
variables.description: Number of days of upstream and route health history to retain.
